classification.difficultyReason: Construct proofs of both rhombus diagonal properties using equal sides, parallel lines and triangle angle sums.

content.prompt: The figure $ABCD$ below is a rhombus.

spec.description: Unshaded rhombus with all four single equality ticks, double parallel arrows on horizontal sides and single parallel arrows on sloping sides. Ordinary source blue ink is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: A upper left, B upper right, C lower right, D lower left; AB parallel DC, AD parallel BC, and all four sides equal. No diagonals are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; diagonals and their intersection are introduced in the solutions.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that each diagonal bisects the two interior angles through which it passes.

answer.short:
$AC$ bisects the angles at $A$ and $C$; $BD$ bisects the angles at $B$ and $D$.

Use alternate angles and the base angles of isosceles triangles.
answer.worked:
Join $AC$. Let $\angle BAC=\alpha$. Since $AB\parallel DC$, $\angle DCA=\alpha$ (alternate angles). Since $AD=DC$, triangle $ADC$ is isosceles, so $\angle DAC=\angle DCA=\alpha$. Thus $AC$ bisects the angle at $A$. Since $AB=BC$, triangle $ABC$ is isosceles, so $\angle BCA=\angle BAC=\alpha=\angle DCA$. Thus $AC$ also bisects the angle at $C$.

Join $BD$. Let $\angle ABD=\beta$. Since $AB\parallel DC$, $\angle BDC=\beta$ (alternate angles). Since $BC=CD$, triangle $BCD$ is isosceles, so $\angle DBC=\angle BDC=\beta$. Thus $BD$ bisects the angle at $B$. Since $AB=AD$, triangle $ABD$ is isosceles, so $\angle ADB=\angle ABD=\beta=\angle BDC$. Thus $BD$ also bisects the angle at $D$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Prove that the diagonals meet at right angles.

answer.short:
$AC\perp BD$.

Use the angle bisections from part a and the angle sum of a triangle.
answer.worked:
Let $AC$ and $BD$ meet at $M$, and let $\angle BAC=\alpha$ and $\angle ABD=\beta$. By part a, $\angle BAD=2\alpha$ and $\angle ABC=2\beta$. Since $AD\parallel BC$, $\angle ADB=\angle DBC=\beta$ (alternate angles and part a).

Using the angle sum of triangle $ABD$:
$$\begin{align*}2\alpha+2\beta&=180^\circ\\\alpha+\beta&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$
In triangle $AMB$, $\angle BAM=\alpha$ and $\angle ABM=\beta$. Hence
$$\begin{align*}\angle AMB&=180^\circ-(\alpha+\beta)\\\angle AMB&=180^\circ-90^\circ\\\angle AMB&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $AC\perp BD$.
